title: Engineering course work experience
titleCn: 工程专业实习经验安排

paragraphs.text: Section three.
You will hear a third-year student talking to a first-year student called David about the work experience David must do as part of his engineering course.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four on page five.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Hi, David. How's the course going?
Oh, good thanks. But I have to start thinking about the work experience component.
Right. So you'll do yours during the holiday, will you?
That's the plan. But I haven't contacted any companies yet. Why do we have to do work experience in the first year? I've got enough on already.

Yeah, the first year's pretty full on. It gets easier once you've chosen the specific area you want to focus on in your second year. But the experience is useful. For a start, you get shown how to use different tools and machines, which you'll probably be using later in an actual job.
Yeah, that'll help.
And everyone working around you will be using engineering language specific to the job and their individual roles.
I guess that helps put it all into context and makes it more meaningful.
Yes, but you're responsible for finding the company, so I'd get on with that. The process takes ages.
So what about you? What criteria did you use to choose a work experience placement?
Well, I knew I wanted to end up in civil engineering, so I applied to a company that I thought I'd like to work for in the future once I finished college, like with a proper contract.
Okay. So I suppose I could choose an employer that wouldn't mind me going back for a second placement in the next long holiday.
Your tutor might not agree to that. They normally like you to go somewhere else for a second placement.
Okay, so what you mean is apply somewhere that I'd actually like to work once I've finished the whole degree. That makes sense.
Some people in my group, I remember, wanted to see what management were doing, but you're unlikely to start off at that level, so...
See what happens at ground level instead. Right, I'll remember that. And I suppose it also needs to be a place where I can see communication between different employees, how they work together.
That's something you have to discuss in the report you write after the work experience is finished. So it's essential, yes.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty on page six.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.
So once you've completed the work experience, you have to write a report. It's about three thousand to five thousand words.
So typed about six or seven pages.

Yes, you print it out and hand it in in a folder and also email a copy. One thing I'd be careful of when you're using a computer, it's really easy to cut and paste paragraphs from different academic sources, and you'll be penalized if you don't acknowledge them.
Fair enough. I'll make sure I make a note of my sources as I go along. What about stuff like photos and diagrams? Do you think the tutor expects to see a lot of those?
Well, only if they're strictly necessary and actually support the points you make. We were told to avoid adding them just for a decorative effect.

And what about the formatting? Is there anything I need to know? I suppose I'd better leave space between paragraphs and keep the margins fairly wide. Otherwise, the tutor won't be able to highlight the problem areas.
Yes, they hate that when there's no room for marking it or to make comments.
Okay.
I'm trying to remember the feedback I had on my report. I think there were a lot of us who had trouble with the section on staffing issues.
The tutor warned us about that. We mustn't forget to describe the way the company is structured. Who's in charge of who, who has responsibility for which department.
That's it. I left that bit out and had to redo it. What were the other sections?
Well, company description. You have to talk about the kind of work that the company does in detail.

That's right. Now make sure you say how what you're doing on the course is connected to the work you observed. Say how it applies to what happens in practice, I mean. Otherwise, the tutor will make you redo that bit.
Yes, he mentioned something about that. And the conclusion, I know they'd like us to put our own opinions in.
But don't be too negative about the company. As far as the tutor's concerned, you don't have the experience to identify any mistakes they're making. Not yet, anyway.
Oh, okay. I won't do that then.
That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
